Here’s a quick snapshot of the most talked‑about crime‑thriller–style flicks that hit theaters (or streaming platforms) during **2020**—the year when Hollywood had to pivot because of COVID‑19, so the slate leaned heavily toward smaller productions and genre hybrids rather than big studio blockbusters.

| Film | Director(s) | Why it counts |
|------|-------------|---------------|
| **“The Invisible Man”** | Leigh Whannell | A modern retelling of H.G. Wells’ classic that blends psychological suspense with techno‑noir vibes. It keeps viewers guessing whether the threat is supernatural or human—and delivers plenty of twists typical of crime‑drama investigations. |
| **“The Invisible Girl”** *(aka “Invisible”) | Alex Karpovsky & Daniel J. Sullivan* | An off‑beat noir mystery where a woman goes missing after being framed for murder. Its low‑budget aesthetic gives it a gritty feel reminiscent of neo‑film noirs, making it a cult favorite among fans of cerebral crime stories. |
| **“The Invisible Woman”** | David Fincher | Though technically a period romance, its investigative plotline around a scandalous affair turns into a tense cat‑and‑mouse game between two lovers trying to keep their secrets hidden—a hallmark of crime‑thrillers. |

> *Note:* Because of the pandemic, many studios postponed larger projects until later years, leaving room for niche filmmakers to experiment within the crime‑thriller framework. If you’re looking for something beyond this handful, consider expanding your scope to early‑2021 releases such as **“The Little Things,” “Nobody,”** or even **“The Irishman.”**

Happy watching!
